overallAssessment.reason: The manuscript now uses only committed official v2 evidence for its policy definition, protocols, tables, figures, and conclusions. It reports the failed repeated validation as a negative result, treats default kube-scheduler as a placement-only external reference, and separates training, repeated validation, and holdout claims.
overallAssessment.preservationDecision: Keep evidence-audit-v1.json and all v1 artifacts immutable as historical pilot evidence. Supersede the manuscript's claims and figures using only committed official v2 artifacts.

findings.title: The manuscript describes the obsolete v1 policy surface

evidence.observation: Official v2 uses nonnegative L1-normalized FreeCPU, FreeMem, Balance, and Consolidation weights. The paper still presents FreeCPU, FreeMem, PodPenalty, and linearly dependent Packing with unnormalized v1 baseline vectors.

findings.requiredAction: Replace the policy definition, equations, baseline names, baseline weights, optimizer representation, and architecture labels with the versioned v2 contract.

findings.title: Optimizer superiority claims are contradicted by repeated validation

evidence.observation: Across eight policies, three training workloads, and ten repetitions per policy-workload, none of the five optimizer finalists survived the repeated-mean Pareto front. All were dominated by balanced or consolidation-heavy baselines.

findings.requiredAction: Remove claims that evolutionary search found a validated regime beyond the baselines. Report the single-evaluation three-seed search as a provisional stage and the failed reproduction as a negative validation result about live-cluster measurement noise.

findings.title: The reported tables and figures are v1 pilot artifacts

evidence.observation: The displayed values come from March 2026 v1 pilot results. Official v2 baselines, repeated finalist validation, uncertainty intervals, requested-load variance, and the holdout Pareto front are not shown.

findings.requiredAction: Regenerate result tables and figures from official v2 summary JSON or CSV. Distinguish single-evaluation search outputs from repeated validation and holdout evidence.

findings.title: Metric names and timestamp semantics are stale

evidence.observation: Official v2 primary latency is high-resolution submission-to-scheduler-decision latency. The consolidation objective is maximum workload-occupied worker nodes, not powered or active infrastructure nodes. Kubernetes condition time and evaluator observation lag are serialized separately.

findings.requiredAction: Use p95 scheduling decision latency and max workload-occupied worker nodes consistently. Define every timestamp source and retain the node metric as a consolidation proxy only.

findings.title: Experimental protocol status is obsolete

evidence.observation: Seeds 42, 123, and 999 are complete; the default kube-scheduler external reference is measured; official workloads contain 24 Pods; official scheduler and evaluator intervals are 250 ms; repeated finalist validation uses n=10; load variance is available; and an independent n=10 holdout is complete.

findings.requiredAction: Rewrite setup and protocol tables from official manifests, including run classes, repetitions, seeds, cadence, versions, and holdout separation.

findings.title: Uncertainty and repeated-validation evidence are absent

evidence.observation: Official summaries report sample standard deviation, extrema, and 95 percent Student-t confidence intervals. Holdout latency intervals overlap substantially even though occupied-worker counts separate at four, three, and two.

findings.requiredAction: Show uncertainty for latency, classify Pareto relations as point-estimate relations, and avoid statistical-superiority language where intervals overlap.

findings.title: Default kube-scheduler is incorrectly described as unmeasured

evidence.observation: The default kube-scheduler was measured for three workloads and three repetitions. It used four workload-occupied workers in all nine runs and completed all Pods, but lacks the custom scheduler's high-resolution decision timestamp.

findings.requiredAction: Include it as an external placement reference. Do not compare custom decision latency directly with unavailable default-scheduler decision latency.

findings.title: The paper does not report the independent holdout result

evidence.observation: The mixed-burst holdout produced three unique repeated-mean Pareto points: spread-heavy at 1.252656 s and four workers, balanced at 1.260228 s and three workers, and consolidation-heavy at 1.304153 s and two workers. Balanced is the preregistered geometric knee.

findings.requiredAction: Make the holdout baseline tradeoff the principal validated Pareto result while stating that optimizer generalization was not evaluated because no optimizer finalist survived train validation.

findings.title: Related-work coverage is too narrow

evidence.observation: The manuscript has six references and no dedicated related-work synthesis for Kubernetes scheduling frameworks, resource-aware placement, multi-objective cloud scheduling, or noisy expensive optimization.

findings.requiredAction: Add a concise related-work section using verified primary papers and official Kubernetes documentation. Do not use discovery-tool metadata without primary-source verification.

findings.title: Workload-aware wording may imply online adaptation

evidence.observation: The system performs offline policy search over a fixed workload suite and does not adapt weights online from a detected workload class.

findings.requiredAction: Define workload-aware as suite-conditioned offline evaluation or adopt a title that says live multi-objective policy search without implying online adaptation.

verifiedOfficialClaims.claim: The v2 policy uses four nonnegative weights normalized to the L1 simplex: FreeCPU, FreeMem, Balance, and Consolidation.
The official baseline protocol contains 36 result rows across three custom policies, default kube-scheduler, three workloads, and three repetitions, with zero unschedulable Pods.
Three official optimizer seeds evaluated 216 optimizer candidates plus nine baseline evaluations, totaling 675 workload executions and 16,200 completed Pods.
None of five optimizer finalists survived the n=10 repeated-mean train Pareto front.
The independent holdout produced three unique baseline Pareto points with four, three, and two workload-occupied workers; balanced is the interior knee.
Every official baseline, optimizer, repeated-finalist, and holdout workload execution completed without unschedulable Pods and retained protocol provenance in committed manifests.
verifiedOfficialClaims.evidence: the four official analysis manifests listed in officialEvidenceSources

gate6Decision.nextAction: Preserve this evidence-closed manuscript as the Gate 6 baseline; future claims require new versioned evidence and a new audit.

resolutions.resolution: Replaced the v1 policy and terminology with normalized FreeCPU, FreeMem, Balance, and Consolidation; defined timestamp and occupancy semantics; removed wording that implied online workload adaptation.

Separated provisional one-shot search from repeated validation and holdout evidence; reported that no optimizer finalist survived; included Student-t confidence intervals and the three-point holdout baseline front.

Replaced all v1 result tables and plots with official v2 baseline, repeated-validation, and holdout artifacts; documented seeds, repetitions, cadence, versions, and default kube-scheduler's placement-only role.
Added a dedicated related-work section with verified primary cluster-scheduling and evolutionary-optimization sources plus official Kubernetes documentation.

checks.visualInspection: all six pages rendered at 150 dpi and inspected; no clipping, overlap, or broken figures; final references balanced with IEEEtriggeratref
checks.numericAudit: paper values and percentages cross-checked against the four official summary JSON artifacts

residualLimitations: kind workers are homogeneous containers on one physical host
default kube-scheduler lacks the custom decision timestamp and is not a latency baseline
holdout evaluates baselines only because no optimizer finalist passed training validation
latency confidence intervals overlap and do not support superiority claims
